title: Pltfm narrowcast - control plane / routing / auth / quotas (weekly check-in)
content:
Date: 2026-12-20
Facilitator: Ava Chen
Duration: 30m (quick sync narrowcast, not a full retro)
Location: Zoom / #pltfm-standup thread

Attendees: Ava, Miguel, Sana, Ravi, Hannah, Joe (joined late), Taylor (ops for quota items)
FYI: This is intentionally short-form; capture decisions + action items.

Topline summary:
- Routing experiment A (weighted fallback) showed ~13% reduction in tail latency for 8k seq; follow-up on cache warm-up needed. (PLAT-4872)
- Auth service saw repeated token refresh errors during load test ramp 2026-12-18 — mitigation in prod is applied, but root cause requires API gateway header handling fix. (PLAT-4901)
- Quotas: soft-quotas rollout for internal teams rolled to 60% of accounts; need clearer user-visible messaging to avoid confusion.

Notes + context:
1) Routing (Miguel)
   - Experiment details: weight-based routing with small-variant fallback when preferred cluster saturated. Ran for 72h on canary traffic.
   - Metrics: p95 decreased from 320ms -> 278ms for long-context generation. Throughput unchanged. Error budget burn lower on canary.
   - Problem observed: cold-KV-cache requests to fallback model had ~2x token-processing CPU bursts during warm-up windows. Likely due to cache miss storm.
   - Quick wins: introduce staggered cache prefetch for fallback pool (Miguel -> prototype by 2026-12-23).
   - Open question: do we include a brief circuit-breaker to prevent oscillation when fallback warms up slowly? (Sana to design simple hysteresis rule).

2) Auth (Sana)
   - Incident recap: token refresh errors at 11:40 UTC on 2026-12-18 during a synthetic load ramp. Symptoms: 401s from gateway; auth-service returning 502 in some cases.
   - Mitigation executed: temporarily increased retry window and bypassed a problematic header validation path. That restored traffic; full fix requires normalize-headers change in gateway.
   - Root cause hypothesis: upstream load balancer sometimes strips empty headers; our header validation treats missing header as malformed token -> rejects instead of accepting.
   - Action: Sana -> RFC for gateway header normalization and a test harness for header permutations (due 2027-01-04).

3) Quotas (Ravi + Taylor)
   - Soft quota rollout: enabled for 60% of internal accounts; telemetry shows a 9% spike in support messages from dev teams who hit unexpected throttles.
   - Messaging gap: UI/console shows generic 429 with no guidance. Need to add contextual message and link to docs with steps and expected behaviors.
   - Action: Ravi -> small UI patch to include quota name and expected retry-after (due 2026-12-28). Taylor -> draft internal comms explaining soft quota semantics (due 2026-12-23).

4) Control plane (Hannah)
   - Control plane deployment model change: rolling coordinator handshake improvement landed in branch; e2e tests flakey in CI when node churn simulated.
   - Observed flakiness trace: coordinator lease renewal sometimes delayed under high GC pause (JVM profiling shows long STW in older JVMs).
   - Decision: proceed with canary on dedicated staging with GC tuning and newer JVM build. Hannah -> run two canaries this week (2026-12-21 and 2026-12-24).

5) Quota enforcement backend cost optimization (Joe)
   - Spike results: switching rate limiter store from Redis sorted sets -> simple token-bucket in-memory backed by replicated write-behind reduces Redis ops by ~45% in the spike harness.
   - Risk: memory growth during bursty traffic; need eviction + telemetry. Joe -> build prototype with metrics and failover test (due 2027-01-07).

Decisions made in this narrowcast:
- Proceed with staggered cache prefetch approach for routing fallback (Miguel).
- Gate header normalization change with test harness before rolling to prod (Sana).
- Add clearer quota messaging in console before expanding soft quotas to more tenants (Ravi + Taylor).

Action items (owner -> due):
- Miguel: prototype staggered KV cache prefetch + experiment plan; due 2026-12-23.
- Sana: RFC + header-permutation test harness for gateway normalization; due 2027-01-04.
- Ravi: UI patch for quota 429 messages (includes 'quota name' + 'retry-after'); due 2026-12-28.
- Taylor: internal comms draft for soft quota rollout; due 2026-12-23.
- Hannah: run controlled canaries with tuned JVM + report flakiness observations; due 2026-12-24.
- Joe: prototype token-bucket limiter with memory eviction and telemetry; due 2027-01-07.
- Ava: schedule a 45m design deep-dive Jan 5 to reconcile routing hysteresis approach with CDNs and knative autoscaling.

Blockers and requests:
- Need SRE capacity to run cross-zone canary for routing fallback (ask: SRE ops slot Friday 2026-12-24).
- Legal/info-sec: confirm no additional user-facing PII appears in new quota messages (Ravi tagged Legal).

Risks / Notes to leadership:
- If header normalization waits beyond Jan, we risk repeated refresh spikes during load ramps — impacts customer SLAs.
- The token-bucket optimization reduces infra cost but introduces memory risk under pathological bursts; require careful chaos testing.

Misc / Notes to self (informal):
- Lunch with infra team next Wed — bring up small infra budget ask for extra canary nodes.
- Reminder: extract experiment dashboard to a shared Grafana panel (less hunting).

Follow-ups for next narrowcast:
- Early signal from Miguel's prefetch prototype (sawtooth in CPU metrics?)
- Result of Hannah's JVM canary runs
- Support ticket trend after Ravi's UI patch

Raw links referenced during meeting:
- PLAT-4872 experiment notes: https://redwood/jira/browse/PLAT-4872
- Auth incident: https://redwood/jira/browse/PLAT-4901
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/612

End of notes.
